title_en: Supreme People's Court Releases Typical Cases on Implementing the Criminal Policy of Combining Leniency with Strictness
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court Publishes Typical Cases on Implementing the Criminal Policy of Combining Leniency with Severity

Case 1:

Zhao Quanxi et al. — Robbery Case

——Robbery causing death, extremely serious consequences and crimes, severe punishment according to law

(I) Basic Facts

Defendant Zhao Quanxi, male, Han ethnicity, born on November 27, 1973, farmer. On December 15, 1994, he was sentenced to 15 years' imprisonment for robbery, and was released upon completion of his sentence on March 23, 2005.

Defendant Miao Kunshan, male, Han ethnicity, born on August 15, 1971, farmer.

In the afternoon of October 27, 2010, after plotting a robbery, defendants Zhao Quanxi and Miao Kunshan carried a green nylon rope purchased by Miao to Longquan Avenue, Xiping County, Henan Province. Pretending to go to the hospital in Chushan Town, Xiping County to pick up a patient, they deceived the victim, Wu Eryou (male, deceased, aged 48), into driving them in his Chang'an Lingyang brand taxi (license plate Yu QT2200, valued at RMB 34,960). When the vehicle reached an unpaved field road north of Changlou Village, Chushan Town, Zhao Quanxi strangled Wu's neck with the nylon rope, demanding money. Miao Kunshan also took out a nylon rope and strangled Wu's neck. Together, they pulled the ropes tightly, causing mechanical asphyxiation death. Fearing Wu might not be dead, Zhao Quanxi tied the nylon rope tightly around Wu's neck. Thereafter, Zhao and Miao threw Wu's body into a ditch by the roadside, seized the taxi, over RMB 240 in cash, and a Nokia brand mobile phone (valued at RMB 138), and fled in the vehicle. During their escape, Zhao and Miao discarded the stolen mobile phone and abandoned the stolen taxi on an unpaved road south of Lilou Village, Yeyi Town, Ye County, Henan Province.

On the afternoon of November 1, 2010, after plotting another robbery, Zhao Quanxi and Miao Kunshan carried a white nylon rope purchased by Zhao to the square of Luohe Railway Station, Henan Province. Pretending to go to Longcheng Town, Yancheng District, Luohe City to collect chicken feathers, they deceived the victim, Wang Guoqing (male, deceased, aged 45), into driving them in his Chang'an Star brand minibus (license plate Yu LFQ565, valued at RMB 33,600). When the vehicle reached a road west of Xiliu Village, Longcheng Town, Miao Kunshan and Zhao Quanxi took turns strangling Wang's neck with the nylon rope, causing mechanical asphyxiation death. Fearing Wang might not be dead, Zhao Quanxi tied the nylon rope tightly around Wang's neck. Thereafter, Zhao and Miao drove the vehicle to a machine-driven well beside the Happiness Canal north of Houzheng Village, Longcheng Town, and threw Wang's body into the well. Zhao and Miao seized the Chang'an Star brand minibus, a Samsung brand mobile phone (valued at RMB 623), and over RMB 720 in cash. After the crime, Zhao and Miao fled to Xiaxian County, Shanxi Province. Unable to sell the stolen minibus, they abandoned it on Bayi Road, Yaofeng Town, Xiaxian County. Zhao sold the stolen Samsung mobile phone for RMB 150 in illegal proceeds.

(II) Judgment

This case was tried at first instance by Luohe Intermediate People's Court of Henan Province and at second instance by the High People's Court of Henan Province. The Supreme People's Lawfully conducted a death penalty review for defendants Zhao Quanxi and Miao Kunshan.

The court held that defendants Zhao Quanxi and Miao Kunshan, with the purpose of illegal possession, used violent means of killing the victims to seize property, and their acts constituted the crime of robbery. Zhao and Miao actively planned the robbery, prepared tools, selected targets, and during the robberies both used nylon ropes to strangle the two victims, jointly strangled them to death, jointly seized property, and disposed of the bodies to cover up their crimes. In the joint crime, both played principal roles and are principal offenders, and should be punished for all crimes they participated in. Zhao Quanxi had previously been sentenced for robbery and, after release, failed to reform, committing robbery again, demonstrating deep subjective malice and high personal danger. Zhao and Miao committed two robberies, with a huge amount of stolen property, caused deaths of two persons during the robberies, with vile nature of crime, cruel means, great social harm, and extremely serious consequences and crimes. Both should be punished according to law. Accordingly, Zhao Quanxi and Miao Kunshan were sentenced to death and the sentences were approved.

Case 2:

Yang Junxiang — Intentional Homicide Case

——Arising from a civil dispute with voluntary surrender, but with particularly serious consequences and crimes, severe punishment according to law

(I) Basic Facts

Defendant Yang Junxiang, male, Han ethnicity, born on October 20, 1965, farmer.

At about 8:00 p.m. on July 24, 2010, when repairing a footpath adjacent to the property of Zhang Shuanglin (male, deceased, aged 36) at Sanwangshe Village, Shimin Village, Xihua Town, Huating County, Gansu Province, Yang Junxiang had a dispute with Zhang Shuanglin and his wife Wang Huirong (deceased, aged 35). Yang struck Zhang on the head once with a pickaxe, knocking him to the ground. When Wang came forward to intervene, Yang struck Wang on the head once with the pickaxe, also knocking her to the ground, and then struck Wang several times on the body with the pickaxe. Thereafter, Yang entered the main room of Zhang's house with the pickaxe, and struck Zhang's father Zhang Jufeng (deceased, aged 63) and son Zhang Ruining (deceased, aged 10) to the ground with the pickaxe, then fled to his home. Wang Huirong died on the way to the hospital after being injured. Zhang Shuanglin, Zhang Jufeng, and Zhang Ruining died at the scene. After committing the crime, Yang asked his brother Yang Xilin to report the case, and police arrived and arrested Yang.

(II) Judgment

This case was tried at first instance by Pingliang Intermediate People's Court of Gansu Province and at second instance by the High People's Court of Gansu Province. The Supreme People's Court lawfully conducted a death penalty review for defendant Yang Junxiang.

The court held that defendant Yang Junxiang failed to properly handle a neighborhood dispute, intentionally and unlawfully deprived others of their lives with weapons, and his act constituted the crime of intentional homicide. Although this case arose from a civil dispute and Yang had the circumstance of voluntary surrender, Yang used a weapon to strike the victims continuously, causing four deaths, with particularly vile circumstances, and particularly serious consequences and crimes. Severe punishment should be imposed according to law. Accordingly, Yang Junxiang was sentenced to death and the sentence was approved.

Case 3:

Zhong Hanyue — Theft Case

——Theft of relative's property with full restitution and obtaining forgiveness, lenient treatment according to law

(I) Basic Facts

Defendant Zhong Hanyue, female, Han ethnicity, born on September 9, 1991, unemployed.

On a certain day in mid-June 2010, when Zhong Hanyue visited the victim Chen Fenhong (Zhong's aunt) at No. 3, 18 Xin Yong'an Road, Shanghai, she discovered and stole an Agricultural Bank of China debit card belonging to Chen from a desk drawer in the shop. On the morning of June 22 of the same month, Zhong, holding the card, went to Shanghai Laofengxiang Silver Mansion at No. 522, Nanjing East Road, Shanghai. By guessing the password and swiping the card, and forging Chen's signature on the sales slips, she purchased three "thousand pure gold repurchase gold bars," spending a total of RMB 128,512.5. Thereafter, Zhong sold the gold bars and used the proceeds to repay her debts to others. On June 27 of the same month, Zhong was arrested and brought to justice. On June 30, with the help of her family, Zhong made full restitution of the stolen money.

(II) Judgment

This case was tried by Huangpu District People's Court of Shanghai. The Supreme People's Court conducted a review of the sentence imposed on defendant Zhong Hanyue below the statutory punishment range.

The court held that defendant Zhong Hanyue, with the purpose of illegal possession, secretly stole another person's credit card and used it, with a particularly large amount, and her act constituted the crime of theft. Given that defendant Zhong voluntarily confessed, actively made full restitution with the help of her family, and obtained full forgiveness from the victim, and comprehensively considering the kinship between the victim and the defendant, as well as the defendant's remorse, a sentence below the statutory punishment range with probation could be imposed on the defendant. Accordingly, Zhong Hanyue was sentenced to and approved for fixed-term imprisonment of three years, suspended for three years.
